# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 11
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## V.1 — "sorely vexed" vs. "greatly displeased" vs. "furious"
- EMET: "greatly displeased"
- LOGOS: "sorely vexed"
- PNEUMA: "furious"
- SOPHIA: "greatly vexed" — Greek *aganaktōn*: irritated/indignant; PNEUMA's "furious" is too strong

## V.2 — "Greek settlement" vs. "colony of Greeks" vs. "Greek city"
- EMET: "Greek settlement"
- LOGOS: "colony of Greeks"
- PNEUMA: "Greek city"
- SOPHIA: "Greek settlement" — Greek *katoikian Hellēnōn*: settlement/colony of Greeks; EMET preferred

## V.3 — "puffed up in his" vs. "puffed up with his" vs. "drunk on his numbers"
- EMET: "puffed up in his" (slightly awkward)
- LOGOS: "puffed up with his" (smoother)
- PNEUMA: "drunk on his numbers" (paraphrase, loses Greek *eparas*)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing retained

## V.5 — "begging the Lord" vs. "beseeching the Lord" vs. "crying out to the Lord"
- EMET: "begging"
- LOGOS: "beseeching"
- PNEUMA: "crying out" (changes the verb entirely)
- SOPHIA: "beseeching" — LOGOS; Greek *deomai*: petition/beseech

## V.6 — "passionate eagerness" vs. "willing eagerness" vs. "burning with eagerness"
- EMET: "passionate eagerness"
- LOGOS: "willing eagerness"
- PNEUMA: "burning with eagerness"
- SOPHIA: "willing eagerness" — Greek *prothymōs*: with readiness/willingness

## V.7 — "brandishing golden weapons" vs. "brandishing golden weapons" vs. "with golden weapons gleaming"
- EMET/LOGOS: "brandishing golden weapons"
- PNEUMA: "with golden weapons gleaming" (participial construction changed)
- SOPHIA: "brandishing golden weapons" — Greek *hopla chrusa prospaiōn*: waving/brandishing golden arms

## V.12 — "loss that had come about" vs. "defeat he had suffered" vs. "what had happened"
- EMET: "the loss that had come about"
- LOGOS: "the defeat he had suffered"
- PNEUMA: "what had happened" (vague)
- SOPHIA: "the defeat he had suffered" — LOGOS; more precise

## V.13 — "settle everything on just terms" vs. "settle everything on equitable terms" vs. "a settlement on fair terms"
- EMET: "just terms"
- LOGOS: "equitable terms"
- PNEUMA: "fair terms"
- SOPHIA: "equitable terms" — Greek *epi tois dikaiois*: on just/equitable conditions; LOGOS preferred

## V.16 — "Senate of the Jews" vs. "council of elders" vs. "council of elders"
- EMET: "Senate" (following some translations)
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "council of elders"
- SOPHIA: "council of elders" — Greek *gerousia*: council of elders; "Senate" is a Latinism

## V.17 — "document written below" vs. "written memorandum" vs. "written requests"
- EMET: "document written below" (odd — no document follows in that verse)
- LOGOS: "written memorandum"
- PNEUMA: "written requests"
- SOPHIA: "written memorandum" — Greek *biblidarion*: little book/memo

## V.22 — "translated to the gods" vs. "passed to the gods" vs. "gone to join the gods"
- EMET: "translated to the gods" (archaic)
- LOGOS: "passed to the gods"
- PNEUMA: "gone to join the gods"
- SOPHIA: "passed to the gods" — euphemism for death; LOGOS most precise

## V.29 — "full amnesty" vs. "full amnesty" vs. "full pardon"
- EMET/LOGOS: "full amnesty"
- PNEUMA: "full pardon"
- SOPHIA: "full amnesty" — Greek *adeian*: safe conduct/amnesty; legal term preferred

## V.36 — "present them in a manner suitable" vs. "advocate them in a manner most advantageous" vs. "put your case in the best possible light"
- EMET: "suitable for you"
- LOGOS: "most advantageous to you"
- PNEUMA: "best possible light"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing — captures the diplomatic/legal register

## V.38 — PNEUMA abbreviates "Make haste" section; all three render essentially the same
- Minor stylistic divergence; SOPHIA follows LOGOS/EMET for formal epistolary register
